notes.fact: AFP reports Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands of homes in Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions; DTEK says over 600,000 residents in Dnipropetrovsk were affected.
notes.key: claim:ukraine dtek power company and local officials
notes.claim_by: party:Ukraine's DTEK power company and local officials

notes.fact: Ukrainian air force data cited by Ukrinform say Russia launched 164 drones since the evening of Nov 7, with 137 neutralised; Ukrinform also reports one person killed in Odesa.
Russia's defence ministry says it hit a power substation in Zhytomyr region that it says served Ukraine's defence industry, plus a container ship southwest of Odesa.
Kyiv Post cites Deputy Energy Minister Nekrasov saying fresh Russian strikes caused outages in seven regions; an analyst says damaged high-voltage lines limit supply to Kyiv.
Newsy Today, citing Zelensky, says Russia used 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles on Kyiv and surrounding region on Nov 7; a key Kyiv bridge was damaged.
Ukrenergo says one of the largest attacks on the grid hit energy sites over 20 times in a day; Kyiv's water supply was cut.
Zelensky says Russia launched 1,940 attack drones, over 1,580 guided bombs and 44 missiles in the preceding week; Ukraine's energy ministry reports outages in eight regions.
CNBC reports Russian strikes cut power to over 350,000 in Dnipro region; a six-day local ceasefire in Kherson appeared to hold, and an Oct 11 energy truce had failed.
Kyiv Independent lists a Komyshuvakha search operation entering a fifth day with the death toll at 53, after a strike on a humanitarian aid centre.
The Hill, citing AP, says rescue efforts at the Komyshuvakha site were hampered by Russian drone attacks, according to military official Mykhailo Semikin.
Meduza reports envoy Witkoff announced trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US talks for Nov 10-11 in Abu Dhabi, with a Brussels meeting with European allies on security guarantees first.
Russian media, per ua.news, say Kremlin spokesman Peskov confirmed Moscow's delegation led by Medinsky will be in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10 and 11.
Kyiv Post says the agenda includes security guarantees and post-war arrangements; earlier rounds in January and February produced no deal but helped with prisoner exchanges.

Latin Times reports the agenda may include a potential energy and maritime ceasefire, prisoner exchanges and return of Ukrainian children; US outlets call earlier rounds constructive without agreements.
TASS reports Russia's defence ministry says it hit a cargo ship carrying military equipment southeast of Odesa, with damage being assessed; no vessel was named.
notes.event: Russian claims of ship strikes off Odesa

notes.fact: SAFETY4SEA reports Russia's defence ministry said it hit a dry cargo ship southeast of Odesa, without naming the vessel, its flag or the damage.
notes.event: Russian claims of ship strikes off Odesa

notes.fact: Clearwater Dynamics, citing open sources, says a Russian drone hit a cargo vessel berthed at Odesa, killing one crew member and wounding three.
notes.event: Ship strikes at Odesa port, autumn

notes.fact: Newsweek says Poland launched a large-scale security operation along its Kaliningrad border this week; ACLED's analyst links it to a wider pattern of Russian hybrid activity.
Lithuania's defence minister told LRT its Kaliningrad border is calmer than Poland's, where Tusk says a potential provocation was thwarted; Lithuanian troop support was extended to mid-November.
Moscow Times reports Lithuania began deploying about 100 soldiers to its Kaliningrad border, citing possible Russian mobilisation and hybrid threats after a Belarus-Latvia border incident.
Ukrainian News, via Europesays, says Moscow recently threatened NATO with force if it tries to isolate Kaliningrad; no date or speaker given.
AP reported Lithuania's president saying intelligence points to possible limited attacks on infrastructure in the Baltics or Poland; the Kremlin dismissed this as a pretext for NATO build-up.
notes.event: Baltic and Polish warnings of provocation

notes.fact: Agenzia Nova reports a drone from Ukraine crossed Moldova over Transnistria at 4:23 and left two minutes later; Moldova recorded 19 airspace violations in October, with six drones exploding.
UA News, citing Moldova's defence ministry, says the Nov 4 overflight came during massive Russian attacks on Ukraine; Moldova's airspace has been violated over 100 times since the war began.
Cotidianul reports another object, not yet confirmed as a drone, was found in woods near Gordinești, Rezina; an explosive Gheran-4 drone crashed near Chiștelnița on Oct 23.
Kyiv Independent reports a drone exploded near Hîrbovăț on Sept 30 with no injuries, and an Aug 17 Russian cruise missile crashed in a Moldovan cornfield.
Euromaidan Press quotes a Ukrainian military analyst linking a drone strike to the opposition's bid to suspend President Sandu; this is one analyst's view, not an established link.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard says two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in or near Hormuz; no maritime authority has confirmed it.
Iranian military said two more tankers caught fire after hitting mines on an 'unauthorised route'. ABC Australia notes the cause of separate blasts on Qeshm was unclear.
Tehran Times (Iranian state-linked) reports the army says Hormuz stays closed until the US accepts Tehran's conditions, and carries the navy's mine-fire claim.
UKMTO recorded 11 attacks on commercial vessels in Hormuz and the Gulf in the seven days to 4 November, according to RFE/RL.
An unnamed US official told AP the Monday strikes hit Iranians firing surface-to-air missiles at US assets. AP says the last known US attacks were in early September.
Gulf News notes Iran is not known to have missiles beyond 2,000 km. That range already covers the Arabian Peninsula, the Levant and parts of Greece.
Iran says Hormuz reopening depends on lifting the blockade, oil-sanctions waivers and a ceasefire including Lebanon. Oman and Qatar held calls with Araghchi; no deal confirmed.
Oman's foreign ministry says it is still working with Iran on a joint Hormuz control arrangement to restore unimpeded traffic.
A US-Iran ceasefire on 7 April and a June memorandum both broke down by July. The US reimposed its blockade after renewed Iranian ship attacks.
Four military sources told Reuters the Houthis are within 80 km (50 miles) of Aden, their closest approach since 2015.
UAE outlet Al-Ain, cited by the Jerusalem Post, reports dozens killed or wounded as Houthis attacked Al-Maqatirah in Lahj. Coalition jets struck back.
CNBC says Saudi authorities did not confirm Houthi attack claims but said they shot down a Houthi drone launched toward the Mecca region.
AFP reported the Houthis attacked Aden after accusing Riyadh of killing 16 in Sanaa and Hodeida; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu.
Gaza's health ministry counts 1,602 Palestinians killed since the October 2025 truce. Five more deaths were reported on Thursday; Israel said it targeted Hamas operatives.
notes.claim_by: party:Gaza health ministry and Israeli military

notes.fact: AFP and Reuters reported at least eight killed in Israeli strikes on 1 November, including five police officers. Israel said it hit militants and disputed some accounts.
notes.claim_by: party:Gaza interior ministry and Israeli military

notes.fact: Al Mayadeen, a Lebanese outlet, put the post-truce toll at 1,610 killed. Rain and sewage flooded Gaza displacement tents.
Israel's army struck Hezbollah sites after drones targeted troops near Ali al-Taher ridge. Katz says Israel stays until Hezbollah is disarmed. No November reports found.
Lebanon's health ministry reported four killed in Israeli strikes on 6 September; President Aoun called it a dangerous escalation. Lebanon puts the death toll since March above 4,300.
notes.claim_by: party:Lebanese health ministry and Israeli military

notes.fact: OCHA counts 377 settler attacks tied to the olive harvest since September, a record since 2006. One Palestinian was killed and over 200 injured.
The UN says at least 160 harvest-linked settler attacks were recorded in the first two weeks of October, often with Israeli forces present or taking part.
OCHA said attacks have reached Areas A and B, with casualty counts differing across sources. One death was counted by OCHA, two by The National.
Iraqi security officials said at least two drones were shot down near the Green Zone, with no damage. The US embassy's air defences were activated.
The Critical Threats project assesses the militias used the drones to surveil the embassy as deterrence. A security source denied they carried explosives.
Sudan's army, via military sources, says it retook Kazgeil and Abu Qaoud, about 45 km south of El Obeid, after clashes with the RSF.
Darfur24 reports the army's allied joint force and the RSF both claimed four areas west and southwest of El Obeid; neither main force confirmed the result.
The joint force's operational commander in Kordofan, Gen. Haroun Mersal, was killed in combat in North Kordofan on 3 November, per a regional situation report.
UN-appointed investigators say RSF drones keep hitting El Obeid's power, water and hospitals; only about 30% of its hospitals work. They also cite arrests by army-linked forces.
notes.key: claim:un independent international fact finding mission for sudan
notes.claim_by: org:UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for the Sudan

notes.fact: Sudan's government says RSF drones hit power stations at Abu Hamad and Al-Dabbah on 1 November, causing local outages; AP is the cited source.
notes.event: Drone strikes on Sudan power grid

notes.fact: A Wikipedia timeline says a drone strike on the Markhiyat power station near Omdurman caused an outage in Khartoum on 27 October, and the Rabak station was hit on 29 October.
notes.outlet: Wikipedia (Timeline of the Sudanese civil war 2026)
notes.event: Drone strikes on Sudan power grid

notes.fact: Sudan's army 4th Infantry Division says it repelled RSF and SPLM-North attacks at Bakori and Sali in Blue Nile; it gave no casualty figures.
The army says RSF fighters defected to it in Damazin, and one commander told it about Ethiopian support for the RSF. The RSF did not comment.
A Blue Nile district governor says about 13 RSF drones hit gold mines, a market, a school and a health centre in Wad Al-Mahi on 29 October.
notes.key: claim:blue nile governor army aligned authority
notes.event: Blue Nile and Kordofan mining-site strikes

notes.fact: US adviser Massad Boulos said 27 countries met in Geneva and urged a humanitarian truce. He said no military solution exists. No date or venue for talks was given.
notes.key: claim:us presidential adviser non combatant mediator

notes.fact: Amani Africa previews AU and EU security councils reaffirming a truce call. It notes the first joint Quintet-Quad meeting on 23 September and a civilian group's objection to excluding the RSF.
Crisis Group says Ethiopian forces took Mekelle on 3 October without a fight, after the TPLF-led alliance's 23 September offensive, and pushed north toward the Eritrean border.
Ethiopia's foreign minister wrote that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray. Eritrea denied backing the TPLF.

A pro-government militia says Eritrean troops retreated with heavy losses; Eritrea's information minister called this false. ACLED recorded federal forces entering Aksum; the casualty claim is unverified.
ACLED recorded Eritrean forces and Tigray Defense Forces leaving Shiraro on 12 October; federal forces reached Zalambessa on the Eritrean border on 13 October.
AFRICOM lists a new airstrike against al-Shabaab on 5 November, in coordination with Somalia's government; it gave no casualty details.
Somali Guardian says some reports link recent US strikes to civilian casualties in Farsoley and Kuntuwarey. Al-Shabaab bars journalists from the areas, so details are unconfirmed.
Congo's army said it retook Uvira after AFC/M23 withdrew; M23 had held the city since 10 December 2025. I found no newer Uvira reporting.
Human Rights Watch says M23 and Rwandan forces committed war crimes in Uvira from 10 December to 17 January, including 62 documented summary executions or unlawful killings.
Open-source tracking says JNIM announced a full blockade of Bamako on 28 April 2026, after an earlier easing in the year.
A risk-intelligence note says Bamako gets fuel only in escorted convoys, more than 300 tankers have been destroyed since 2025, and the junta's Russian and Turkish support has not lifted the blockade.
A Substack analysis says Mali's army and Russia's Africa Corps left Kidal, Tessalit and other northern posts after the 25 April JNIM and FLA offensive. Unverified here.
Taiwan's defence ministry counted 49 PLA aircraft in the 24 hours to 6am Nov 3, this year's highest daily total. The count fell to 22 the next morning.
notes.event: PLA air surge near Taiwan, Nov 3

notes.fact: Taiwan accused the China Coast Guard of harassing ships off its east coast and asserting fictional jurisdiction there; Taiwan's coast guard sent vessels to shadow the Chinese ships.
notes.event: China coast guard patrols off Taiwan east coast

notes.fact: Taiwan's coast guard says China has increased east-coast patrols since June; Taiwanese officials worry this could prepare for a blockade, though that is their reading.
notes.event: Taiwan blockade concern, east coast patrols

notes.fact: A tracking site reports PLA aircraft in Taiwan's zone fell 52% in Jan–early Aug 2026 versus 2025, while navy sightings fell only 7%.
Manila says it tracked 101 Chinese navy and coast guard ships in September, up from 56 in August, per a Philippine military tally.
The Philippine coast guard says a Chinese vessel used a water cannon to try to stop a patrol ship fetching a sick sailor at Second Thomas Shoal.
The Philippine coast guard says a Chinese cutter rammed the fisheries vessel Magat Salamat 54 nautical miles off Palawan; no injuries were reported.
notes.event: Ramming of Philippine fisheries vessel, Sept 18

notes.fact: China's coast guard says the Philippine ship cut across its bow and blamed Manila; the US ambassador condemned the ramming.
notes.event: Ramming of Philippine fisheries vessel, Sept 18

notes.fact: CNN's crew was aboard a Philippine vessel hit by Chinese water cannon at Scarborough Shoal; China's state broadcaster says its coast guard took lawful measures.
China's foreign ministry says Tokyo alone is responsible for poor ties and is evading the issue; Takaichi still refuses to retract her Nov 2025 remarks.
The Japan Times says the two economies are moving toward selective dependence after China imposed export restrictions on Japan following Takaichi's remarks.
Ukrainian outlet Mezha, summarising Japanese reporting, says Japan-China ties show little sign of a thaw a year on, with the dispute unresolved.
South Korea's defence ministry says North Korea fired multiple missiles from the Sondok area toward the east coast sea, its fourth launch in a month.
Japan's defence ministry issued no alert, which suggests the weapons could have been artillery or shorter-range missiles, according to the Japan Times.
North Korea's state media says it tested a new anti-aircraft missile and held a cruise missile strike drill on Nov 4; Seoul's military said missile types were still being analysed.
A South Korean unification ministry official said the launches were largely a response to the Freedom Flag allied air exercise; the paper counts four launches since Oct 29.
Kim Yo Jong ruled out dialogue with Washington until the US drops its 'hostile policy' and again denied North Korea stole Binance crypto.
The FBI attributed the theft of over $6bn in crypto from Binance to North Korean hackers; Pyongyang called this a 'trite provocation'.
Seoul says North Korea laid mines south of the border line that injured South Korean soldiers in September; Pyongyang denies it. Reports say two or three soldiers were hurt.
Pakistani and Afghan border forces traded fire on Sunday Nov 1; Torkham shut about five hours, and one civilian died in mortar fire near Angoor Adda.

The Pakistani army spokesman says talks held this year with China's involvement produced no breakthrough, and that September saw Pakistani airstrikes in border areas after attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
China said both sides agreed in Urumqi, after seven days of talks, not to escalate; fighting since February had killed hundreds, it said.
Pakistan's army media wing says troops killed 17 militants in Kachhi and Kharan on Nov 1 and lost one soldier; independent confirmation was not found.
Pakistan's army statement blames India-backed groups for the Balochistan militants, an accusation that India has not been shown to confirm in these reports.
Pakistan's military says nine militants were killed in Kachhi and Wadh districts on Oct 26.
The Arakan Army says Myanmar air strikes on Nov 1 killed at least 12 civilians and injured 32 across Kyauktaw, Mrauk-U, Pauktaw and Kyaukphyu.
A news report counts 15 killed in Rakhine air strikes on Sunday, including a newborn, as the Arakan Army advances toward Sittwe.
The ULA initially reported 49 civilians killed in the Sept 28 Kyauktaw strike, and Development Media Group later put the toll at 50.
A resistance newsletter says the Arakan Army attacked the Shwemingan naval base near Sittwe on Nov 6 and that the junta massed about 7,000 troops in the city; both unverified.
As of 2026 Sittwe is the only settlement in northern Rakhine still under junta control, per this summary page; it has not fallen.
notes.event: Sittwe is last junta-held town in north Rakhine

notes.fact: Haiti's national police say a joint operation in Cité Soleil fatally wounded Boston gang leader Mathias Saintil, as 2,000+ Salvadoran troops and private contractors join the fight, Bloomberg reports.
Rio Times says Haiti's government announced Saintil's death. It notes the UN counts at least 26 gangs near the capital and the UN-backed force's mandate runs to 31 March 2027.
Haitian police found the burned truck used by the four missing Salvadoran technicians in Croix-des-Bouquets on 3 November; the men themselves have not been found.
Taipei Times reports the UN says most Salvadoran personnel operate outside the UN-backed force, which works with Haitian police, the army and the private firm Vectus Global.
HaitiLibre reports a Salvadoran official saying troops have cleared parts of Croix-des-Bouquets; the outlet notes no independent count of gang dead exists.
Hundreds of residents in Port-au-Prince, Belladère and Jérémie marched in support of Bukele and Salvadoran troops, citing low trust in Haitian security institutions.
Democracy Now relays the NYT: four US officials say the US gave Venezuela's military drones and intelligence for a deadly attack on the ELN on 30 October.
Venezuelanalysis says NYT and WSJ suggest US forces piloted the drones, though the NYT was unclear who flew them; Venezuela's government and military have not commented.
Venezuelan rights group Fundaredes reported 23 killed in the 30 October Apure strike; the US role and the full toll are not independently established, the outlet says.

Colombia's defence ministry says the first air strike under President De la Espriella killed two presumed ELN members in San Calixto; the ombudsman reported displacement and three civilians were injured.
notes.event: Colombian air strike on ELN, Catatumbo

notes.fact: US officials told the NYT the State Department is negotiating a status-of-forces agreement with Venezuela; one said base talks are far off, with no numbers or locations set.
Rubio told the NYT Washington wants a presence agreement letting US troops operate jointly with Venezuela, The Center Square reports; Trump left open the idea of bases.
Security chief García Harfuch said soldiers shot at while patrolling Navolato, Sinaloa, killed three gunmen and seized rifles and a vehicle; a drug lab was also dismantled in Puebla.
Rio Times notes the dead were not named, no group was linked to them, and Sinaloa remains the centre of a split between Sinaloa Cartel factions.
García Harfuch said Navy personnel killed Cártel de Guasave operator Jesús González Peñuelas, with a US $5m reward, in Sinaloa on 26 October; forensic ID was still pending.
The US military said a strike on an alleged drug boat in the eastern Pacific killed five; the AP counts at least 240 dead since September 2025.
notes.event: US strike in eastern Pacific, 27 Oct

notes.fact: Wikipedia's running tally lists 80 strikes, with the latest on 27 October and 243 dead including 17 missing; it also lists September boardings of vessels.
notes.event: US strike in eastern Pacific, 27 Oct

notes.fact: InsightCrime reports a deadly Caribbean strike on 4 October, following two lethal and seven non-lethal strikes in September.
Ecuador began its fourth curfew of 2026, midnight to 5am until 10 November in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas, with police and army raids on gangs.
Diario las Américas says special operations had detained 218 people, and that homicides averaged over 20 a day from January to September.
President Noboa said the September curfew cut crime 40% and that weekly homicides fell from 146 to 111 across weeks 39 to 42; no independent data was cited.
Ecuador recorded 9,283 homicides in 2025, a record; local elections are set for 29 November, per EFE via Bolivia's Red Uno.
The State Department says it designated ten targets, including a Cuban oil shipping network and China-based military suppliers, and listed five vessels as blocked property.
Infobae reports food, medicine and medical equipment trade stays authorised, and general blackouts have recurred in Cuba since March.
The Hill says Rubio offered Cubans a CIA partnership in late October and that Trump signalled plans for military action against the island; no deployment is reported.
Wikipedia's page says the US has blocked tankers bound for Cuba since February 2026, with tariff threats on oil suppliers; Cuba had talks with Washington in March.
Cuban authorities blame US sanctions for severe outages and fuel scarcity, some lasting over 24 hours; Washington blames Cuban economic policy, per yourNEWS.
Al Jazeera reports that on Nov 2 fridges and freezers at over 100 shops in several European countries ran hot, with no clear culprit.
Reuters reports the Nov 2 attack hit Ahold Delhaize, Colruyt, ICA and Coop, and at least some units used Danish maker Danfoss controllers also hit in France.
NBC News reports temperature spikes and spoiled food at stores in Sweden, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg and Estonia, following a similar attack in France.
RTÉ says Ireland's cyber centre confirmed Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell controllers were compromised; pro-Russian groups claimed a Danfoss attack, but a link to the supermarket hacks is unproven.
Axios quotes a former FBI cyber official calling Russia a reasonable first suspect, and notes SentinelOne says Russian-aligned hackers previously claimed fridge attacks in Europe.
SentinelOne says Russian-aligned groups CARR, NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest are credible suspects, but the evidence does not yet show who is responsible for the European incidents.
Cybernews says Forescout found nearly 13,000 vulnerable refrigeration systems in 99 countries and over 20 claimed Russia-linked hacktivist attacks on cold storage since January 2026.
Help Net Security says three French blood banks caught and reversed a temperature spike after a cyberattack on a refrigeration supplier to the blood service EFS.
HIPAA Journal says French blood-bank cold rooms had temperature and defrost settings altered remotely, but staff acted in time to prevent loss of blood products.
CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a fact sheet on ongoing attacks on industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems, urging operators to act now.
Infosecurity Magazine says the advisory lists steps: take controllers off the internet, change default passwords, isolate OT networks, use multi-factor authentication, patch and keep offline backups.
Defense One says the US notice does not name a culprit, and that the EU Commission, ENISA, Europol and national agencies issued their own joint warning on Wednesday Nov 4.
Wikipedia says Ahold Delhaize's US chains Stop & Shop and Food Lion reported IT disruptions; the entry's link to the fridge hacks is not confirmed by other sources found.
Defense One reports, citing two unnamed people, that US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers caused freezer failures at about six military commissaries since late August.
NPR says investigators treat the commissary outages as a cyberattack with some evidence pointing to Iran, but with low confidence in that attribution so far.
Fish4News says the Pentagon has not confirmed Iran or hacking as the cause, and the controller makes, models and intrusion method have not been publicly established.
Nextgov reports Cyber Command and defence law-enforcement units are probing the commissary incidents with French authorities; a Fort Huachuca freezer entered defrost mode on Aug 26.

CBS reported in early August that over 30 Minnesota water systems were hit via internet-exposed controllers, with Iran only one suspect and no public attribution; CISA urged removing exposed controllers from the internet.
Sweden Herald, citing Der Spiegel, says two Belarusians were held for a planned attack on a rail station near Nuremberg; Romanian intelligence says a Moscow-run network is behind related arson.
Finland sentenced a Russian captain to 3.5 years and an Azeri sailor to 2 years 10 months over anchor damage to a cable in December 2025; the ruling can be appealed.
TechRepublic reports Binance traced the $6.3bn theft to malware from a fake job-interview task; the FBI attributes it to North Korea-linked TraderTraitor.
eSecurityPlanet reports attackers compromised 996 Zyxel GS1900 switches in 48 countries via a zero-day, and the campaign continued after an earlier patch.
Cybersecurity Dive reports an AI-enabled campaign chained flaws to compromise Palo Alto firewalls at about two dozen targets, including sites linked to the US government.
notes.hotspot: cyber: new: Palo Alto firewall chain

notes.fact: Industrial Cyber's news list says ESET uncovered Gorbag, a cyberespionage campaign targeting Ukrainian administrations, the defence sector and a transport hub; no state attribution is stated.
